chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: The merger of the Black and white musicians' unions
summary: The merged 802 opened downtown hotel jobs to Black musicians that white contractors had controlled.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: When was that black union, say, phased out, or when did it join 802? Was this before you got to New York or was it sometime during --
I think it was before I came to New York.

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.
WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

Yeah, because the time (that) (inaudible) of the union they had a -- the same thing was happening in Philly. They were trying to get the black union and the white union together. They held out for a long time before they got together. And all through the west, because I remember one time we played with Chick in Oklahoma. The white union and the colored union just had went together. And when the union went together in New York, the guys found out they could get gigs all downtown, because the whiteys had them blocked out. Because all their jobs used to come in through the union. And they had guys that are contractors and things for the hotels. And they were the ones getting all these jobs (inaudible). Less somebody call you, they call you at the Rhythm Club and got you into that, you were just blocked out. So when they merged together, it was

much better for the colored union -- musicians. So they began to get gigs all over.
